issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-5a0dc962 (umbrella). Depends on the build-from-archive.sh child.

Add a test that snapshots "git stash list" and "git reflog" in the shared checkout immediately before and after a full scripts/build-from-archive.sh run and asserts both outputs are unchanged. This encodes the parent's acceptance criterion that a run never mutates the shared checkout.

Acceptance:
- The test runs the script end to end and fails if the shared checkout's stash list or reflog changes
- The test asserts the scratch dir is removed on success and retained on failure
- Failure output names which shared-checkout state changed, so a violation is diagnosable without re-running
issue.notes:
Shipped: tests/build_from_archive_checkout_untouched.rs (commit 9b24591, pushed 63c2ee8..9b24591).

All three acceptance lines pinned:
- Success run is a full end-to-end `scripts/build-from-archive.sh <HEAD sha>` (git-archive extraction + `cargo build --release`, ~2 min) with snapshots of `git stash list`, `git reflog` and `git rev-parse HEAD` taken immediately before and after; any difference fails the test, and the panic names WHICH state changed and prints both snapshots. HEAD is compared directly because this checkout's reflog is legitimately empty (expired during the 2026-09-01/02 incident recovery), which would make a reflog-only comparison vacuous.
- Scratch lifecycle: on success no new entry may remain under ~/scratch; on a failing build the scratch dir must remain. The failure input is a valid sha plus `--features` with a value no package has — cargo rejects that after the archive is extracted and the scratch dir exists, before anything compiles, so the failing path is fast and deterministic. The test removes its retained dir after asserting, so the shared ~/scratch does not accumulate per run.
- Both runs pass `--out` into a throwaway TMPDIR dir, so a test run never leaves pin artifacts in pinned-binaries/ for the next worker's `git status`.

Verified live 2026-09-02 ~20:15 EDT against scripts/build-from-archive.sh as it stood in the shared tree (beadrs-53e55a45's work, uncommitted at that time): `2 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 115.67s`. rustfmt --check clean; clippy silent on the test target. The failure plumbing was exercised for real twice during development (a newline-terminated sha arg made both tests fail loudly with the script's stderr inline). The test skips loudly while the script has no committed form, so a fresh checkout/CI stays green until beadrs-53e55a45 lands; from then on it runs in every `cargo test`.

Ops note for whoever staged files around 20:19 EDT: the shared git index held four staged files from another worker (AGENTS.md, BUILD_PROCEDURE.md, docs/pinned-binaries.md, pinned-binaries/COMMITS.md); my first commit swept them in, I repaired immediately with `git reset --soft HEAD~1` + `git restore --staged` (no worktree content touched) and recommitted as 9b24591 with only the test file. Those four files are back UNSTAGED, byte-identical — re-add them before committing.

Re-verified live 2026-09-03 (beadrs-3804efb4 retry/dispatch): scripts/build-from-archive.sh has now landed (9e7745c, amended by 8d2e4be), so the test's skip-guard is inactive and both tests exercised the real end-to-end path (git-archive extraction + cargo build --release) against the committed script: `2 passed; 0 failed; ... finished in 125.35s` under the local cgroup fallback (TMPDIR=/var/tmp/beadrs-3804-tmp). Pin out dirs cleaned, no new entries left under ~/scratch, shared-checkout snapshots equal. No file changes needed — the test shipped at 9b24591 and is byte-identical in the working tree.
